title: Invisible Worker - Shared Data Contracts (v1)
description: Canonical shapes for the Invisible Worker probabilistic ledger. Flow: raw TransactionEvent(s) are fused into one balanced LedgerEntry; unrecorded stock loss on an inventory account is explained by a LossDistribution. Conventions: (1) Money is non-negative and expressed in major currency units; debit/credit carries direction, never a minus sign. (2) Uncertainty is mean +/- std_dev (1 sigma); the approximate 95% band is mean +/- 1.96 sigma. (3) wall_clock is untrusted - 1970 or future resets are valid input - so all ordering uses (logical_clock, device_id, id). (4) IDs are RFC 4122 UUIDs; field names are snake_case. (5) additionalProperties is false everywhere, so extend this schema deliberately instead of smuggling extra fields. To validate an instance, resolve against {"$ref": "#/$defs/<Type>"} (TransactionEvent, LedgerEntry or LossDistribution).

Account.description: Double-entry account path using ':' as the hierarchy separator. Examples: 'Cash', 'Inventory:Tomatoes', 'Udhaar:Sharma ji', 'Expenses:Spoilage'. Segments may use any script and may contain spaces; empty segments are invalid. Debit and credit accounts within one entry must differ.

TransactionEvent.title: Transaction Event (raw evidence)
TransactionEvent.description: One unmerged capture from one channel. Several events may describe the same real-world transaction; fusing them is the engine's job. Raw events are append-only: never edit or delete one, and never overwrite raw_text after a Lexicon Drop. Re-interpretation produces a new event or a new fusion, preserving auditability.

event_id.description: RFC 4122 UUID generated on the capturing device. Globally unique; used for provenance, de-duplication and fusion bookkeeping.

device_id.description: CRDT actor ID of the capturing device, e.g. 'device-a'. Together with logical_clock it gives a total order that survives hostile wall clocks.

source.description: Capture channel. audio = ambient speech transcript; ocr = text read from a photo or slip; sms = delayed SMS chime or pasted SMS; manual = quick-tally keypad.

raw_text.description: Verbatim transcript, OCR output, SMS body or typed tally before normalization or lexicon mapping. May be empty if nothing was legible (see confidence). Never rewritten; re-process with a newer lexicon instead.

wall_clock.description: Device-reported capture time as ISO 8601 with offset. UNTRUSTED: a 1970 reset or a timestamp in the future is valid input. Never order history by this field alone.

logical_clock.description: Lamport counter maintained by device_id. The canonical ordering key is (logical_clock, device_id, event_id), so delayed SMS messages and out-of-order delivery cannot reorder history.

confidence.description: Probability that the capture is intelligible and correctly transcribed, given noise, blur, oil stains and compression. 0..1.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code for every price in extracted_entities, e.g. 'INR'. Prices use major units: 180.0 means 180 rupees, not paise.

extracted_entities.description: Structured lines the extractor could parse. May be partial or empty: clauses that were heard but not understood (for example a customer-credit phrase such as 'Sharma ji ka 40 jama kar') remain only in raw_text until a Lexicon Drop maps them.

language.description: Optional BCP-47 tag of the dominant language, e.g. 'hi-IN' or 'en-IN'.

media_ref.description: Optional device-local URI or path to the original audio/photo for audit and re-processing. Not synced by value.

lexicon_id.description: Optional ID of the Lexicon Drop snapshot applied when interpreting raw_text. Replaying with a newer lexicon must create a new interpretation, never mutate this event.

examples.raw_text: Bhai 3 kilo tamatar liya 180 mein... Sharma ji ka 40 jama kar, aur 7 plate poha de.

ExtractedEntity.title: Extracted Entity (one evidence line)
ExtractedEntity.description: One item/quantity/price line parsed from an event. A line may be uncertain; price = null means the extractor recognized an item but no legible price, which must never be coerced to zero.

item.description: Item token exactly as captured, before canonicalization, e.g. 'tamatar' or 'tomato'. Canonical English account names belong in the ledger, not here.

qty.description: Quantity in unit. Floats are allowed because portion sizes and non-standard units fluctuate.

unit.description: Unit token exactly as captured, e.g. 'kg', 'kilo', 'peti', 'dozen' or 'plate'. Normalization to a canonical unit is engine-side; the raw token is preserved.

price.description: Extended line price (qty x unit price) in the event currency's major units. null = missing or illegible; never treat null as 0.0.

confidence.description: Optional per-line extraction confidence. Consumers fall back to the event-level confidence when absent.

raw_span.description: Optional [start, end) character offsets into the parent raw_text, used for audit and UI highlighting.

LedgerEntry.title: Ledger Entry (probabilistic double-entry posting)
LedgerEntry.description: The fused, balanced output of the probabilistic engine: exactly one transaction and one CRDT document per real-world event. Engine-enforced invariants that JSON Schema cannot compare: debit.amount_mean == credit.amount_mean within 0.01, debit.amount_std_dev == credit.amount_std_dev, debit.account != credit.account, and every event_id resolves to an existing TransactionEvent. Conflicting replicas of the same transaction_id are resolved deterministically by highest (logical_clock, device_id); a reversal is a new version with status = voided, never a deletion.

transaction_id.description: Stable ID of the fused transaction; the CRDT document key. The same real transaction keeps the same ID on every device.

status.description: pending = single-event estimate awaiting corroboration; fused = two or more events merged; posted = committed to the canonical ledger; voided = reversed but retained as a tombstone for audit.

confidence.description: Overall confidence that this entry reflects the real-world transaction. Usually lower than the best individual source event because fusion accounts for disagreement.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency shared by both postings, e.g. 'INR'.

event_ids.description: Provenance: every TransactionEvent fused into this entry, in any order. Unique so no evidence is counted twice (prevents triple-counting across audio, OCR and SMS).

logical_clock.description: Lamport clock at fusion; it must be greater than every source event's logical_clock. The ordering key is (logical_clock, device_id, transaction_id).

device_id.description: CRDT actor ID of the device that authored this fused entry, e.g. 'device-a'.

business_date.description: Optional accounting date (YYYY-MM-DD) reconstructed from logical order, never from wall_clock. Used for daily accrual profit.

created_at.description: Optional timestamp of when the engine produced this entry. Informational only; it is not an ordering key.

clock_suspect.description: Optional flag set when any source wall_clock is implausible (before 2000-01-01 or more than 24 hours in the future). Drives the warning icon in the UI; ordering still uses logical_clock.

loss_distribution_id.description: Optional link to the LossDistribution attributed to this entry.

lexicon_ids.description: Optional list of Lexicon Drop snapshots that influenced the interpretation of the fused events.

notes.description: Optional human-readable note, e.g. why a piece of evidence was rejected.

Posting.title: Posting (one side of a double-entry transaction)
Posting.description: A probabilistic account posting. mean +/- std_dev is a 1-sigma band, so the approximate 95% interval is mean +/- 1.96 sigma. Amounts are non-negative: the debit/credit side carries direction. Quantity fields are optional and belong only to quantity-bearing accounts such as Inventory.

amount_mean.description: Expected amount in the parent entry's currency, major units (180.0 = 180 rupees).

amount_std_dev.description: 1-sigma uncertainty of the amount. Use 0.0 only for genuinely known amounts, such as cash physically counted.

qty_mean.description: Optional expected quantity for quantity-bearing accounts. Omit for Cash.

qty_std_dev.description: Optional 1-sigma uncertainty of the quantity. Must not appear without qty_mean and unit.

unit.description: Canonical unit for the qty fields, e.g. 'kg'. Required whenever qty_mean is present.

LossDistribution.title: Loss Distribution (attribution of unrecorded stock loss)
LossDistribution.description: Probabilistic split of unexplained inventory loss into spoilage, theft and personal consumption, conditioned on environmental covariates. The distribution is Dirichlet over cause shares; qty_lost and value_lost describe the magnitude. Engine-enforced invariants that JSON Schema cannot sum: share_mean values sum to 1.0 (+/- 0.001), each cause appears exactly once, alpha has one positive entry per component in the same order, and value_lost quantiles satisfy q05 <= q50 <= q95 when present.

loss_distribution_id.description: Stable ID of this computed estimate.

transaction_id.description: Optional link to a single LedgerEntry when the loss belongs to one purchase. Omit for period-level reconciliation; then period is required.

account.description: Inventory (or expense) account whose loss is attributed, e.g. 'Inventory:Tomatoes'.

period.description: Optional reconciliation window for aggregate losses. Required unless transaction_id is present.

qty_lost.description: Estimated unrecorded quantity. Both mean and std_dev are non-negative.

value_lost.description: Monetary value of the loss in parent currency major units. mean +/- std_dev is the primary interval; q05, q50 and q95 are optional percentiles.

components.description: Exactly one component per cause: spoilage, theft and personal_consumption, in any order. share_mean values form a probability simplex over the three causes.

covariates.description: Drivers used by the attribution model. The known keys are listed; extra scalar keys are allowed for future covariates.

expected_sales_units.description: Recipe-inference forecast; a shortfall raises the probability of theft or personal consumption.

allocation.description: Generative model for the cause shares. A larger sum(alpha) means a tighter, more confident split.

alpha.description: Dirichlet concentration parameters in the same order as components. Expected share_i = alpha_i / sum(alpha).

confidence.description: Confidence in the attribution as a whole. 0..1.

evidence_event_ids.description: Raw events (purchases, sales, stock counts, SMS) that fed the estimate. No duplicates.

method.description: How the split was produced. dirichlet_bayesian is the default; monte_carlo records a simulation result that was fitted back to Dirichlet parameters.

computed_at.description: When the estimate was computed. Informational; it is not an ordering key for ledger history.

model_version.description: Version of the attribution model and covariate mapping, e.g. 'loss-attribution-v1.0'.

explanation.description: Optional one-line human summary for the dashboard tooltip, e.g. 'Spoilage dominates: 34C heat and 9h unrefrigerated.'

components.driver: 34C heat and 9h unrefrigerated; tomatoes lose about 8% per day.
4 fewer plate-sales than expected, yet no stock remained on hand.
Household meals draw from the same tomato stock.

examples.explanation: Spoilage dominates: 34C heat and 9h unrefrigerated, plus 4 fewer plate-sales than expected.

LossComponent.title: Loss Component (one attributed cause)
LossComponent.description: Fraction of unrecorded stock loss attributed to one cause. Across the three components the shares form a probability distribution that sums to 1.

cause.description: spoilage = rot, pest or handling loss; theft = third-party removal; personal_consumption = stock used by the vendor's household instead of being sold.

share_mean.description: Expected share of total loss. share_mean values across the three components sum to 1.0.

share_std_dev.description: 1-sigma uncertainty of the share. Values above 0.5 are impossible for a variable confined to [0, 1].

driver.description: Short causal explanation shown in the UI tooltip, e.g. 'High spoilage due to 34C heat'.

ProfitSummary.title: Profit Summary (true accrual profit for one period)
ProfitSummary.description: Dashboard summary for one business day or period. Profit is accrual-based, not cash on hand: profit_mean = revenue_mean - cogs_mean - loss_mean (within rounding). All values are in the vendor's local currency major units. Uncertainty is 1 sigma, so the approximate 95% band is mean +/- 1.96 std_dev.

revenue_mean.description: Expected sales revenue for the period.

cogs_mean.description: Expected cost of goods actually consumed or sold (not merely purchased), inferred without a formal Bill of Materials.

loss_mean.description: Expected value of unrecorded stock loss (spoilage + theft + personal consumption).

profit_mean.description: Expected true accrual profit. May be negative.

profit_std_dev.description: 1-sigma uncertainty of profit, combining revenue, COGS and loss uncertainty.

time_period.description: Business day this summary covers, formatted YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. '2026-10-25'.

RecipeBurnRate.title: Recipe Burn Rate (inferred ingredient use per serving)
RecipeBurnRate.description: Zero-shot recipe inference result: how much of one ingredient is used per single plate or cup, inferred from purchases, sales and wastage without a Bill of Materials. To display a per-40-plates figure, multiply qty_per_plate_mean and qty_per_plate_std_dev by 40.

dish_name.description: Dish or drink name, e.g. 'Poha' or 'Chai'.

qty_per_plate_mean.description: Expected quantity of this ingredient used per one plate or cup, in unit.

unit.description: Canonical unit of the per-serving quantity, e.g. 'kg' or 'L'.

confidence.description: Confidence that the inferred burn rate is close to the true recipe.

explanation.description: Plain-language basis for the inference, e.g. 'About 2.1 kg per 40 plates, from purchases vs. plates sold.'

examples.explanation: About 2.1 kg +/- 0.3 kg per 40 plates, inferred from 84 kg purchased vs. 1,600 plates sold over 20 days.

CustomerCredit.title: Customer Credit (implicit udhaar balance for one alias)
CustomerCredit.description: Reconciled credit for one customer alias. balance_mean is the expected outstanding balance: positive means the customer owes the vendor, negative means the customer has paid in advance. Uncertainty is 1 sigma, so the approximate 95% band is balance_mean +/- 1.96 balance_std_dev.

customer_alias.description: Local alias or name used for this customer, e.g. 'Sharma ji'. Aliases are reconciled to one customer by the engine.

balance_mean.description: Expected outstanding balance in major currency units. Positive = customer owes vendor; negative = advance paid.

confidence.description: Confidence that the alias and balance are correctly reconciled.

LexiconEntry.title: Lexicon Entry (one taught local word or unit)
LexiconEntry.description: A single Lexicon Drop correction. Entries are versioned: a correction to an existing term creates a higher version, and older versions are retained for audit. Raw TransactionEvents are never rewritten; re-interpretation uses the newer version.

local_term.description: Local word or unit as heard or read, e.g. 'jama kar', 'peti' or 'tamatar'.

corrected_meaning.description: Canonical meaning, e.g. 'Record as Customer Credit (Udhaar)'.

category.description: How the term changes interpretation: credit = money owed/paid; purchase = a buying phrase; unit = measurement unit; item = item name.

version.description: Version of this term's meaning. Starts at 1 and increases with each correction.

DeviceSyncState.title: Device Sync State (one family device)
DeviceSyncState.description: Sync status for one of the family devices. last_merged_logical_clock is the highest Lamport counter this device has merged, and is the only ordering signal the UI should trust. conflicts_resolved counts contradictory ledger entries merged deterministically without data loss.

status.description: Connection state shown on the Device Topology screen.

last_merged_logical_clock.description: Highest logical clock this device has merged. Never use wall clocks for this.

conflicts_resolved.description: Number of conflicting ledger entries resolved without data loss.

MergeResult.title: Merge Result (three-device CRDT sync)
MergeResult.description: Outcome of one network sync. Devices are the post-merge sync states, merge_log explains each deterministic step, ledger_after_merge is the deduplicated ledger in (logical_clock, device_id, transaction_id) order, and conflicts_resolved counts contradictory replicas resolved without dropping a transaction.

merge_log: Device device-a (clock 45) merged with Device device-b (clock 45): 2 conflicts, 0 losses
Merged result (clock 46) merged with Device device-c (clock 45): 1 conflict, 0 losses
Final: 3 devices, 3 total entries, 3 conflicts resolved

ClockResetResult.title: Clock Reset Result (hostile wall-clock recovery)
ClockResetResult.description: Result of simulating a device whose wall clock was reset to 1970. The offending value is reported separately; the entry is appended and ordered by the logical clock, and the previous history is retained.

examples.message: Hostile clock detected on device-b. Wall clock ignored. Entry reordered by logical clock 45. No history lost, no double-counting.
merge_log: device-b wall clock 1970-01-01T00:00:00+05:30 is implausible; logical clock 45 assigned.
Device device-b (clock 46) merged with Device device-a (clock 45): 0 conflicts, 0 losses
Merged result (clock 47) merged with Device device-c (clock 45): 0 conflicts, 0 losses
Final: 4 entries in logical-clock order; 0 history lost.

ledger_after_merge.notes: Simulated hostile-clock sync probe; not a real purchase.

EntryExplanation.title: Entry Explanation (auditable fusion receipt)
EntryExplanation.description: Human- and machine-readable explanation of one ledger entry. Shows the stored value, the evidence lines, the price-agreement verdict, the exact uncertainty adjustment, and per-source counterfactual ranges from the reproducible Monte Carlo run.

examples.narrative: Audio and OCR agree on Rs 180. The two-source fusion applies a 15% range discount. The OCR wall clock reads 1970, so it is used as evidence but ignored for ordering. This canonical entry is pinned to the demo seed; the live simulation produces approximately Rs 180 +/- Rs 29.44.

DailyTruth.title: Daily Truth (ghost inventory + profit autopsy)
DailyTruth.description: One-screen reconciliation of physical stock against purchases and recipe consumption, combined with the live loss split and the accrual-profit waterfall. The ledger_fingerprint is a SHA-256 over the canonically serialized, logically sorted ledger.

loss_components.driver: 34C heat and 9h unrefrigerated; tomatoes lose about 8% per day.
4 fewer plate-sales than expected, yet no stock remained on hand.
Household meals draw from the same tomato stock.

reconciliation.method: purchases minus recipe consumption vs physical stock count

actions: Keep tomatoes shaded: spoilage is about 55% of the modelled loss.
Confirm about 0.23 kg of household use with the family.
The physical gap is within 1 sigma of the model; no large theft signal.
examples.narrative: You bought 3.0 kg of tomatoes and 7 poha plates use 0.105 kg by recipe. Expected on hand is 2.895 kg, but 2.1 kg was counted, so 0.795 kg (Rs 47.7) is missing. The model expects 0.9 +/- 0.25 kg, so the count is consistent. True profit after hidden loss is Rs 1200 +/- Rs 179.51.
